summary: chai-tracker spawns hidden subprocess loading undocumented peer dependency dbconnectify on plugin registration
details: chai-tracker is a fork of chai-spies (identical author metadata, README, and lib layout) republished under a lookalike name. lib/spy.js adds an assertConnection() helper that spawns a Node child process via spawn(process.execPath, ['-e', code],...) whose inline code requires the peer dependency `dbconnectify` and invokes `queryDBConnect()`. assertConnection() is called at the top level of the plugin, so `chai.use(require('chai-tracker'))` triggers execution of dbconnectify's code inside an isolated subprocess. The README advertises the package solely as a chai spies plugin and does not mention dbconnectify or any subprocess/database behavior. package.json declares `dbconnectify: ^1.0.1` as a peerDependency, making dbconnectify the actual payload delivery vehicle while chai-tracker acts as the loader.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
